text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday, prepared for Reuters by the Estonian news agency, ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Police in the eastern Viru county opened a criminal case of embezzlement for 1.78 million kroons against well-known businessman Priit Saksing, a former director of the rare metals plant Silmet.

- The government is prepared to continue negotiations over a minimum wage, Prime Minister Mart Siimann said after a meeting with trade unions but declined to mention any figures. Trade unions demand 1,200 kroons from January 1, 1998.
- The Estonian National Olympic Committee is to elect a new president.
- A tenant in a house in a Tallinn suburb who threatened the owner and his workmen with a pistol in August, was ordered to pay a 4,400 kroon fine.
- Estonia should concentrate on officer training and not spend resources on secondary aims, said Danish commander of armed forces, Christian Hvidt.
- Tallinn Cable Network bought new equipment worth 250 million kroons and plans to offer a wide range of phone and TV services to 180,000 households.
- Leading ministry officials are still getting extra pay for belonging to the boards of state-owned companies, although the law that prohibits this came into force seven months ago.
